artifacts.summary: Verifies task 121's stated precondition against the live source store; finds test/lint retargeting incomplete and the live /research|/plan|/implement --hard command surface still dependent on the files this task would delete.

next_steps: Do not proceed to planning/implementation. Either reorder the backlog so Task 124 (delete lifecycle commands) lands before this task, or split this task's scope: fix lint-contract-compliance.sh Checks A/C/E and lint-agent-contracts.sh's in-scope path list now (independently needed regardless of sequencing), and defer file/agent deletion plus manifest routing_hard removal until Task 124 has landed.

memory_candidates.content: Before trusting a task-status label of [COMPLETED] for a retargeting/migration task, verify the actual file content against the specific claims in its own completion summary -- task 120 ("Retarget hard mode tests to engine branch") claimed lint-contract-compliance.sh was fully retargeted, but git-show of its own cited commit (f3fb615bb) shows only Check D and Check C's trailing sub-block were touched; Checks A, C's main loop, and E still hard-require the files a sibling deletion task targets. A completion summary describing intent is not proof of the diff's actual scope -- read the commit.

In this repo's core-agent-system consolidation backlog, a task's stated `Dependencies` list in TODO.md is not a complete safety net for a deletion task's precondition -- task 121 (delete hard-mode lifecycle files) lists dependencies 118/119/120/128 only, omitting task 124 (delete /research /plan /implement commands), even though those commands' live --hard flag still routes to the exact files task 121 deletes via command-route-skill.sh and each manifest's routing_hard block. Always trace actual live callers (grep for the skill/agent name across commands/, scripts/, manifests) rather than trusting the dependency list alone when verifying a deletion task's stated precondition.
